title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 84-86): Grothendieck is axiomatizing a 'tame' analysis situs. There is a set \u2131 of 'figures' (pp. 84-86) carrying two partial orders. G \u2264 F means G is a subfigure (closed part) of F. G \u227c F means G is a subdivision (refinement) of F; this reading is supported by p. 86, where F'_i is 'une subdivision de F_i' and is restricted to F_i \u2229 F_j.

The axioms on p. 84 are as follows.
(a) Unique restriction of subdivisions: given a subdivision G of F and a subfigure F' \u2264 F, there is a unique G' \u2264 G with G' \u227c F'. G' is the 'restriction' G|F'.
(b) Extension of subdivisions, not necessarily unique: a subdivision of a subfigure G \u2264 F extends to a subdivision F' of F containing it.
(c) A non-degeneracy condition: F \u2264 G \u227c F implies F = G.

Grothendieck then defines the composite relation G \u226a F \u21d4 \u2203F' with G \u2264 F' \u227c F ('G is a subfigure of some subdivision of F'). He states that \u226a is a partial order, using only a) and b). Axiom a) works as a 'distributive law' letting a \u2264-step followed by a \u227c-step be rewritten in the other order, which gives transitivity.

This page continues the Remark.
(ii) The square produced by a), with F' \u2264 F, G \u227c F, G' \u2264 G, G' \u227c F', is cartesian for \u226a: G' = Inf_\u226a(F', G). Thus the restricted subdivision is the \u226a-meet of the subfigure and the subdivision.
(iii) If a square of \u2264-relations (F \u2265 G, F \u2265 F', F' \u2265 G', G \u2265 G') is cartesian for \u2264, i.e. G' = F' \u2227 G, then it remains cartesian for \u226a. In other words, \u2264-intersections are also \u226a-meets.
No proofs are given.

A margin note says many properties of Inf/Sup are missing and should be deduced from the axioms.

The rest of the page is a programme for the axiom list. It should include:
- a block of axioms about \u2264 alone (C1-C4);
- a whole group of 'formal' properties linking \u2264 and \u227c, without questions of support or disjunction;
- a minimal catalogue for \u2264 alone;
- conditions ensuring that Inf and Sup, when they exist for \u2264, commute (a distributivity question);
- induction on a subdivision.
The page ends with the aim of extracting 'minimal axioms' that yield the bulk of the 'obvious' formal properties of the geometric situations.

The next page (86) carries this out with axiom C8 (gluing of subdivisions), the corollary Subdiv(\u2210F_i) \u2245 \u220f Subdiv(F_i), and the start of the disjunction/support axioms.
errors: (ii) and (iii) are asserted without proof. Proving the meet property in (ii) needs, for any H \u226a F', H \u226a G, a factorization H \u2264 K \u227c G'. This seems to require using a) repeatedly and c), and possibly more than a), b), c). The page itself flags (margin) that properties of Inf are missing and must be derived, so this is a gap acknowledged by the author rather than an error.
The notation for the vertical relations in the squares is ambiguous (\u2228| vs \u227c). The reading 'G subdivision of F' is inferred from context (p. 86) and is not stated explicitly on this page.

ideas.what: Poset of figures with two orders (subfigure \u2264, subdivision \u227c), and the composite order \u226a = \u2264\u2218\u227c made transitive by a unique-restriction square axiom
ideas.modern_name: Composite of two relations via a distributive-law / factorization-system-like condition; restriction of subdivisions (cf. stratifications, cell decompositions, PL subdivision theory)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in PL topology (restriction and extension of subdivisions); the abstract form is akin to factorization systems (Freyd-Kelly 1972) and distributive laws (Beck 1969)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), \u00a75-6, without this axiomatics

ideas.what: Restricted subdivision equals the \u226a-meet; \u2264-cartesian squares remain \u226a-cartesian
ideas.modern_name: Pullback/meet stability (Beck-Chevalley-type) for two classes of morphisms

ideas.what: Programme of minimal axioms for the 'formal' properties of tame geometric figures: \u2264 alone (C1-C4), \u2264/\u227c interaction, commutation of Inf/Sup, induction on subdivisions, then support/disjunction axioms
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic tame topology; closest notions are o-minimal structures (van den Dries, Pillay-Steinhorn, Knight) and axiomatic stratification theory (Shiota's subanalytic/semialgebraic theory)
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries et al. (o-minimality, 1980s-1998); Shiota (1997)
ideas.where_published: Only the general wish is in Esquisse d'un programme \u00a75-6

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to axiomatize tame topology purely order-theoretically. He uses a lattice-like structure of figures with a subfigure order and a subdivision order, linked by restriction/extension squares, rather than definable-set structures as in o-minimality. He explicitly leaves open which minimal axioms yield the formal properties, including when Inf/Sup commute and induction on subdivisions. To my knowledge this 'two-order' axiomatics of figures and subdivisions has not been developed in the literature, which went the model-theoretic (o-minimal) route instead.
missed.quote: Au besoin, ... de dégager les axiomes minimaux donnant le gros des propriétés formelles "évidentes" ... géom.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An order-theoretic or categorical axiomatics of 'figures + subdivisions' could give a synthetic, model-independent framework for tame geometry. Such a framework might connect to constructible sheaves, exit-path categories and combinatorial models of stratified spaces, but its content here is only programmatic.

deep.surprise_reason: The concrete statements (composite order, meet property of restricted subdivisions) are routine order theory. The interest lies only in documenting Grothendieck's unpublished attempt at an abstract axiomatics of tame topology, which is programmatic and unfinished.
transcription_corrections: 'sans question de rapport ou de dispersion' should likely read 'sans question de support ou de disjonction' (cf. p. 86 'Axiomes de disjonction et de support').
'des ptés de nos significations géom.' is more likely 'des ptés de nos situations géom.'.
'un axiome concernant \u2264 tout seul' may read 'un regroupement concernant \u2264 tout seul (C1 à C4)'.
'Dans les axiomes des critiques' is uncertain; likely 'Dans les axiomes des C...' referring to the numbered axioms C1-C8.
'(sont-elles prises vraies d'équivalence)' is uncertain; possibly '(sauf celles qui ne sont qu'équivalences)'.
'l'induction sur une ... subdivision' is plausibly 'l'induction sur une subdivision'.
